substitutions.pattern: Resume an existing subagent only when the work needs state that lives in it and is costly to move: its checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs.
substitutions.replacement:
Send a follow-up to an existing child (`t3_thread_send` to its `childThreadId`) only when the work needs state that lives in it and is costly to move: its checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs.

**Dispatch on T3.** Every subagent is a `delegate_task` call from the chat that runs the playbook, same model family included, so every child shows up in T3. When you are a `delegate_task` child, you are a leaf. Do the work yourself, and start no subagent unless your brief names one. Give each call its own `clientRequestId`, stable across retries of that call, and keep each returned `taskId`. A child's completion wakes this thread, so end the turn instead of polling, and call `task_status` only when a result is needed mid-turn. `task_cancel` stops a child, and `task_status` confirms it stopped. A child gets only its brief, never your context, so pass absolute paths. `<plugin root>` is the absolute path of the directory that holds this plugin's `skills/` and `agents/`. A persona (`poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko`, `thermo-nuclear-review-subagent`, `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review-subagent`) is a brief whose line after the `worker.md` line reads "Read `<plugin root>/agents/<name>.md` in full and act as it says", and a `poteto-agent` brief also names this file's absolute path.

A child starts in your checkout, which suits one writer while you write nothing. A writer that runs beside other writers or your own edits gets `isolation: "worktree"`, and T3 gives it a new worktree and branch from your thread's checkout at its `HEAD` commit. Commit what it builds on first, because uncommitted edits stay behind. A child that must start from another commit, such as a PR head or fresh trunk, gets `isolation: "worktree"` even when it only reads. Its brief names that commit or ref, and before anything else the child runs `git fetch` and moves its own branch there with `git reset --hard`. T3 can rename that branch during the run, so the brief tells the child to end its reply with the output of `pwd`, `git branch --show-current`, and `git rev-parse HEAD`. After review, bring its commits onto your branch with `git merge <branch>`, which fast-forwards when your branch has not moved. A PR opens only from a T3 thread's branch, yours or that of a child that owns the PR. In a repo with no commit yet, `delegate_task` refuses the worktree with `Unable to resolve the parent checkout commit`, so commit first. When this thread's project is not a git checkout, which gets the same refusal, when your work lives in a checkout other than the one `t3_worktree_status` names, or when you copy uncommitted changes into the child's worktree, create that worktree with `git worktree add` from `HEAD` instead. Remove that worktree and its branch after the result. A child sent into a worktree it does not own, one you made this way or one a finished worker left, keeps `isolation: "shared"`. Its brief names that absolute path as the only place it writes, and tells it to run every command there (`workdir` on Codex) and to edit by absolute path. Record your own `git status --porcelain` before you dispatch a writer to another checkout, and check after the result that it is unchanged. A step a playbook says to delegate goes to `delegate_task` on that role's sheet entry, not into your own tool calls, unless you state a reason such as a step too small to brief. A research delegate no role names runs on the `judgment and prose` entry. A model's family is the first segment of its ID's last `/` part, such as `claude`, `gpt`, or `grok`, whatever provider instance serves it, and your own family is the one in `orchestrator_capabilities`' `inheritedModel`. A rejected target runs on another target of the same family from `orchestrator_capabilities`, and you say so. `orchestrator_capabilities` lists a short set of models per provider, and its `search` finds the others. A required review with no reviewer from another family stays `BLOCKED: independent review`.

End every reply that ran a playbook with a dispatch ledger: one line per delegated step, naming the role and the `providerInstanceId/model` it ran on, or `in-thread: <reason>`.
substitutions.rationale: inserts the T3 dispatch policy at the end of the Subagents section (Tool actions; Subagent policy). A delegate_task child keeps delegate_task, so the leaf sentence stops the session-start routing from sending a child into a playbook's fan-out (#21). A writer gets T3's worktree isolation, which starts from the thread checkout's HEAD commit and refuses a thread whose project is not a git checkout or has no commit, so git worktree add stays only for those (#50). A child whose worktree gets uncommitted changes copied in, as interrogate's adversaries do, needs that fallback too, because isolation leaves uncommitted edits out. Isolation always starts at the parent's HEAD, so a child bound for a PR head or fresh trunk fetches and resets its own branch there, a child sent into a worktree it does not own works there by path, and the report names pwd so a parent learns a worktree it could not name at spawn (Cursor Bugbot on #68). Tool actions: Continue a subagent. Upstream's worker.md line opens every kickoff, so a persona's line comes after it

substitutions.pattern: Read the whole transcript.
substitutions.replacement:
Read the whole transcript, this conversation's own, where this thread's host keeps it. Do not search other projects' transcripts, which belong to unrelated chats.

On Claude Code, run the finder with this session's ID, this project's transcripts directory, and a fragment of the conversation's opening user prompt:

```bash
node "<plugin root>/skills/reflect/scripts/find-transcript.mjs" --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/<encoded-cwd>" "<opening prompt fragment>"
```

`<plugin root>` is the directory that holds this plugin's `skills/`, and `<encoded-cwd>` is what `node -p 'process.cwd().normalize("NFC").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-")'` prints in the directory Claude Code started in, which is that directory's physical path with every character other than an ASCII letter or digit turned into `-`. If the result is longer than 200 characters, Claude Code keeps the first 200 and appends `-` and a hash, so use the folder under `projects/` whose name starts with those 200 characters and that holds this session's transcript. With the session ID set, the finder prints this session's own transcript, and exits 1 when it does not exist, because a scan could return a sibling session that shares the opening prompt. Without it, the finder scans the flat, nested, and subagent layouts newest first and prints the first transcript whose opening typed prompt carries the fragment. Do not reimplement the scan by hand.

On Codex, pass this thread's ID, which Codex exports as `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, to the resolver, and never search by chat title or time:

```bash
"<plugin root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/resolve-codex-transcript" "$CODEX_THREAD_ID"
```

On success it exits 0 and prints JSON whose `path` is the transcript. If either command exits non-zero, read the conversation as your context holds it, and say so.

substitutions.replacement: Each owner is a `delegate_task` child with `mode: "async"` and `isolation: "worktree"` that starts from fresh trunk, per poteto-mode's Dispatch on T3. Its brief names this playbook and this thread's ID, so the owner reports back with `t3_thread_send`. It also tells the owner that it is not a leaf and starts the subagents its playbooks name, such as `/no-comments`'s Comment Sicko and show-me-your-work's cross-model review of the trail, because Dispatch on T3 makes a child a leaf unless its brief names its subagents. T3 starts a top-level thread only when the user asks for one, so each PR owner is a delegate_task child in its own T3 worktree, which task_status and task_cancel reach (#47, by @pb3975). A child is a leaf unless its brief names its subagents, so the owner's brief says in plain words that the owner is not a leaf and names the reviewers its playbooks start. 2.2.6 said only that the brief lets the owner delegate, and in a proof run the root wrote 'You are a leaf' into the owner's brief, so the owner ran Comment Sicko's pass itself and skipped the trail review. T3 gives a delegate_task child no watch_pull_request, so the root holds the watch an owner's wait for a person needs. Isolation starts at the root's HEAD, which need not be trunk, so the owner resets its own branch to fresh trunk

substitutions.pattern: In `check` mode pass `--status-only`.
substitutions.replacement: In `check` mode pass `--status-only --timeout 120 --max-query-errors 2`, which returns inside the 600-second tool cap. Run `drive` as a loop inside the turn: run the watcher with `--timeout 540` and the shell's own timeout above 540 seconds and under the 600-second tool cap, act on its verdict, and run it again. Report and stop when the verdict's head SHA, kind, and reason have not changed for two hours, or after three hours in all. A `BLOCKER` with reason `review-required` or `merge-blocked` (exit 6) needs a person, so report it and stop the loop instead of rerunning the watcher. `review-required` is the wait for a human review below, and `merge-blocked`, a branch protection rule the watcher cannot name, goes back to the user. A wait for a human review is `watch_pull_request` and the end of the turn, because another account's review wakes the thread. Unwatch with `unwatch_pull_request` when babysitting stops. The watcher holds `READY` until accounts other than the PR author and the `gh` viewer have been quiet on the PR for `--settle` seconds (default 300) since the latest push, opening, or ready for review, and up to 30 minutes after that while an `eyes` reaction is open, so no per-bot wait rules are needed.
substitutions.rationale: Playbooks: Babysit check. Upstream's babysit has no drive step left to anchor on, so the T3 drive loop follows the check-mode flags: the watcher loops inside the turn, the watch-pr settle overlay (t3-pstack 1.0.5), and the exit 6 merge gates from pstack-claude #95 (t3-pstack 2.0.0-rc.2)
